name: CAPE VERDE

flag.title: Cabo Verde Flag
flag.note: Blue seas, red-white path, ten island stars

lead: Cape Verde is ten volcanic islands in the Atlantic Ocean, 570 km off West Africa. Nobody lived here until Portuguese sailors arrived in 1460. So its people and songs mix Africa, Europe and the sea.

sections.geography: A land of fire & desert winds

geo: The ten islands form two groups. Sal and Boa Vista in the east are flat, with sandy dunes. Santo Antão and Fogo in the west have jagged peaks.
Fogo is an active volcano. It last erupted in 2014 and buried a whole village in lava. Now farmers grow coffee and grapes inside the crater.
animals: Cape Verde has one of the world's largest loggerhead turtle nesting colonies. Boa Vista's beaches see over 170,000 nests in a single season. Each August, mother turtles come ashore at night to lay eggs.
The Raso lark lives only on one tiny islet. The whole species would fit inside a football stadium. Humpback whales pass by in winter.
culture: Morna is a slow, soulful music of longing and the sea. UNESCO added it to its heritage list in 2019. Cesária Évora, the 'Barefoot Diva' from Mindelo, took it to concert halls worldwide.
Cachupa is the national stew of corn and beans, simmered with fish or meat. Each February, Mindelo holds a colourful carnival parade.
history: Before 1460 the islands were empty. Portuguese explorers built a colony that became West Africa's first big trading hub. Sadly, it was also a key stop in the slave trade.
Cape Verde was Portuguese for 500 years. Amílcar Cabral inspired the independence movement. Freedom came through talks after Portugal's 1974 revolution. Independence Day is 5 July 1975.
wows: Cape Verde has no rivers, so most islands make fresh water from seawater.
Cesária Évora's face is on the 2,000 escudo note.
Pico do Fogo erupted in 2014, and people now farm inside the lava field.
Cape Verde has never had a military coup.
Trade winds blow so hard that some trees grow sideways.
More Cape Verdeans live abroad than on the islands.
In the 1800s Mindelo was a busy coal stop for steam ships.

myths.myth: Cape Verde means the islands are green
myths.fact: The name comes from Cap-Vert, a green point on the Senegal coast. The islands themselves are mostly dry.
Whales are mammals. They breathe air and feed their babies milk. Humpbacks sing long songs.
